# ui::TextInteraction

Header: `winui/ui/text/Inlines.hpp`.

Selection and link state over laid-out inline text, shared by [TextControl](../controls/text.md#uitextcontrol), [RichText](../controls/rich-text.md#uirichtext) and [RichTextOverflow](../controls/rich-text.md#uirichtextoverflow). Offsets are the [TextLayout](../rendering/text-layout.md)'s. A [RichText](../controls/rich-text.md#uirichtext) and its overflow containers each have their own layout over the same content, so they share one selection.

A building block for a custom text element. Keep one as a member and pass it the element's pointer and key events together with its [TextLayout](../rendering/text-layout.md). Redraw when it reports a change, and let it fill the layout's paint when rendering.

Example: 
```cpp
class Article : public ui::Element
{
protected:
    bool pointer_override(const ui::PointerEvent& e) override
    {
        const bool held = interaction_.pressed_link || interaction_.dragging;
        if (interaction_.pointer(e, layout_, ui::Point{bounds().x, bounds().y}, 0, bounds(), true, links_))
        {
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Visual);
        }
        return held || interaction_.pressed_link || interaction_.dragging; // a link or selection press
    }
    bool key_override(const ui::KeyEvent& e) override
    {
        const bool acted = interaction_.key(e, layout_);
        if (acted)
        {
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Visual);
        }
        return acted;
    }
    // Programmatic selection: interaction_.select(0, 5); interaction_.selected_text(layout_);

private:
    ui::TextLayout                 layout_;
    ui::TextInteraction            interaction_;
    std::vector<const ui::Inline*> links_; // from to_layout_paragraphs()
};
```

## anchor

```cpp
std::size_t anchor = 0
```

Where the selection started (the fixed end), as a layout offset.

## caret

```cpp
std::size_t caret = 0
```

The moving end of the selection, as a layout offset; equal to [`anchor`](#anchor) when nothing is selected.

## dragging

```cpp
bool dragging = false
```

Whether a selection drag is in progress.

## hover_link

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> hover_link {}
```

The index of the link under the pointer; unset when there is none.

## pressed_link


The index of the link pressed and not yet released; unset when there is none.

## select

```cpp

```

Selects the layout offsets [begin, end); `end` becomes the caret.

## pointer

```cpp
bool pointer(const PointerEvent& e, const TextLayout& layout, Point origin, std::size_t first_line, const Rect& bounds, bool selectable, const std::vector<const Inline*>& links, bool sole_view = true)
```

Handles pointer input over `layout`. The top of the first drawn line sits at `origin`, and `first_line` is the layout line drawn there. A press on a link arms it, and a release on the same link invokes it. Elsewhere, when `selectable`, a press places the selection and a drag extends it. A double click selects the word, a triple click the paragraph, and Shift extends. `sole_view` means the layout is the content's only view, so a drag carries on past its edges. One of several linked views, such as a [RichText](../controls/rich-text.md#uirichtext) and its overflow containers, only follows the pointer while it is over that view. Returns whether anything visible changed.

## key

```cpp
bool key(const KeyEvent& e, const TextLayout& layout)
```

Ctrl+A selects everything, and Ctrl+C copies the selection to [ui::clipboard()](namespace-ui.md#clipboard). Returns whether it acted.

## context_menu

```cpp
void context_menu(Point anchor_point, const TextLayout& layout, ContextMenuHost& host)
```

Shows the context menu of a selectable text block, with Copy and Select All.

## selected_text

```cpp
std::string selected_text(const TextLayout& layout) const
```

The selected text as UTF-8 (empty without a selection).

## paint

```cpp
void paint(TextLayout::Paint& paint, const Theme& theme, bool show_selection, std::optional<Color> highlight) const
```

Fills the paint's link colors, and its selection when `show_selection`. The paint keeps a pointer to this object and to `theme` for the duration of the render.
